hints.content: Let's perform each of the sequences and see if they map $\triangle PQR$ onto $\triangle ABC$.

In Sequence A we perform a $180\degree$ rotation about point $R$...



[[☃ image 1]]

...then a translation $2$ units to the right and $6$ units up.



[[☃ image 2]]

We can see that this sequence does *not* map $\triangle PQR$ onto $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: The first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C has point A at nine, fourteen, point B at twelve, ten, and Point C at eight, ten. The pre-image of triangle P Q R has point P at five, eight, point Q at two, four, and point R at six, four. It is rotated one hundred eighty degrees about point R to form the image of triangle P Q R has point P at ten, four, point Q at seven, zero, and point R at six, four.

The first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C has point A at nine, fourteen, point B at twelve, ten, and Point C at eight, ten. The pre-image of triangle P Q R has point P at ten, four, point Q at seven, zero, and point R at six, four. The image of triangle P Q R has point P at twelve, ten, point Q at nine, six, and point R at eight, ten. There is a green line that highlight the shift two units right and six units up.

hints.content:
In Sequence B we perform a translation $4$ units to the right and $6$ units up...



[[☃ image 1]]

...then a reflection over the horizontal line through point $A$.



[[☃ image 2]]

We can see that this sequence does *not* map $\triangle PQR$ onto $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: The first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C has point A at nine, fourteen, point B at twelve, ten, and Point C at eight, ten. The pre-image of triangle P Q R has point P at five, eight, point Q at two, four, and point R at six, four. The image of triangle P Q R has point P at nine, fourteen, point Q at six, ten, and point R at ten, ten. There is a green line that highlight the shift four units right and six units up.

The first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C has point A at nine, fourteen, point B at twelve, ten, and Point C at eight, ten. The pre-image of triangle P Q R has point P at nine, fourteen, point Q at six, ten, and point R at ten, ten. It is reflected over a horizontal line that passes through point A making a triangle P Q R that is above triangle A B C instead of mapping onto it.

hints.content:
In conclusion, neither of the sequences maps $\triangle PQR$ onto $\triangle ABC$.

*Note:* There are many possible combinations of transformations that would map the figure onto the image.

question.content:
Triangles $\triangle PQR$ and $\triangle ABC$ are congruent. The side length of each square on the grid is $1$ unit.



[[☃ image 1]]

**Which of the following sequences of transformations maps $\triangle PQR$ onto $\triangle ABC$?**

Sequence A | Sequence B
:- | :-
A $180\degree$ rotation about point $R$, then a translation $2$ units to the right and $6$ units up. | A translation $4$ units to the right and $6$ units up, then a reflection over the horizontal line through point $A$.

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: The first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C has point A at nine, fourteen, point B at twelve, ten, and Point C at eight, ten. Triangle P Q R has point P at five, eight, point Q at two, four, and point R at six, four.
